dedupe_keys.name: waterplein benthemplein floodable water square rotterdam

description: The Benthemplein water square in Rotterdam's Zomerhofkwartier (ZoHo) district combines public space and stormwater storage in one place, as part of the city's strategy to increase climate resilience through adaptive measures. Three basins collect rainwater: two shallow basins receive water from the immediate surroundings whenever it rains, and one deeper basin fills only in persistent rain with water gathered from the wider area; large stainless steel gutters carry rainwater across the square into the basins, and the water is then conveyed to the city's open water system. Most of the time the square is dry and used for sport, play and events, with amphitheatre-style seating. It covers one square in central Rotterdam, designed in 2011 to 2012 and completed in 2013 by De Urbanisten for the Rotterdam Climate Initiative and the City of Rotterdam, supported by the Schieland and Krimpenerwaard water board, and was largely financed by water management budgets and innovation subsidies after participatory workshops with local schools, a church and residents. The project pages are free to read online; Project for Public Spaces describes it as the start of Rotterdam's first climate-proof district. Caveats: the pages read give no storage volumes or monitored performance, so the case is descriptive. It is useful as a reference design for climate adaptation and green-blue stormwater infrastructure in dense cities; a related record is the London green infrastructure framework.
